title: Marginea black pottery
summary: Marginea in northern Romania is known for black pottery: jars thrown from local clay, burnished with a smooth stone and smoked in a closed kiln until they turn black. Here you throw a jar, then mark its bands in burnished and matte black with a little ochre.
howToPlay: Look at the small jar in the frame: that is the shape to make.
Drag across the spinning clay, row by row, to set the width of the jar; the lit outline shows the target.
Pick a finish from the swatches and tap a band: burnished strokes, incised lines or an ochre slip, as on the target.
Press Check to see your stars.
rules: The jar has twelve rows; each row can be set from narrow to wide.
Shape counts for most of the score, the finish of the bands for the rest.
Each band must carry the finish shown on the target.
Undo takes back your last change; Reshape returns to the clay.
Three stars for a close shape with every band in the right finish.
heritageNote: At Marginea in Bukovina, northern Romania, potters have long fired their ware in a kiln that is closed off so the smoke blackens the clay. Before firing the surface is burnished with a smooth pebble, and many pots carry incised wave and zigzag lines. The craft is still practised in the village.
